newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HILL LEADS PISTONS PAST HURTING ROCKETS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HILL LEADS PISTONS PAST HURTING ROCKETS.

text.p: The hurting Houston Rockets head into the All-Star break grateful for a chance to lick their wounds, while the Detroit Pistons head in celebrating their return to elite status in the NBA.
The Pistons posted a 96-87 victory over the Rockets Thursday as Grant Hill scored 16 points and dished out eight assists and Terry Mills added 16 points and nine rebounds.
The win gave the Pistons a 34-12 record at the break, third best in the league behind only the mighty Chicago Bulls and the Miami Heat.
Otis Thorpe chipped in 14 points and 12 boards for Detroit, which has won six of its last seven games.

"That was a great win for us and a great way for us to go into the All-Star break," said Detroit coach Doug Collins. "We took advantage of an undermanned team and a tired team. But those are the games you have to do that."

Hakeem Olajuwon scored 18 points and Kevin Willis had 17 for Houston, which has dropped a season-high six in a row. The team was without starters Charles Barkley and Clyde Drexler, who both had to bow out of the All-Star Game due to injury.
"We're a hurt team right now," said Houston coach Rudy Tomjanovich. "When we get everyone back, we'll have a good shot at the title."
Houston, 32-16, has fallen 1 1/2 games behind Utah in the Midwest Division.

"We're a team that can potentially win the whole thing," said Willis. "Once we get going again, we'll be all right. This a good time for the break. We just have to stay together and keep confident in ourselves."
In Miami, Voshon Lenard recorded a career high for the second straight game with 38 points and the Heat topped the Milwaukee Bucks 102-90 for their sixth consecutive win.
Lenard's performance came on the heels of his 28-point effort in Wednesday's 118-117 victory at Boston. Lenard's offensive outburst included six three-pointers.

Tim Hardaway had 22 points and nine assists for the Heat (36-12), who were without starting centre Alonzo Mourning because of a bruised heel. Mourning also will miss Sunday's All-Star Game. Isaac Austin, starting in place of Mourning, had 14 points and 12 rebounds.

Johnny Newman, starting in place of the ailing Glenn Robinson, scored 26 points to lead the Bucks, who have lost five straight. Vin Baker added 23 points and 14 rebounds. Robinson was sidelined with a case of the flu.
Miami leads the Atlantic Division, two games ahead of the Knicks.
In New York, Allan Houston scored 22 points as the Knicks coasted to a 96-84 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.
Larry Johnson scored 20 points for the Knicks, who improved to 3-1 without injured centre Patrick Ewing, who will miss the All-Star Game with a strained groin.

Buck Williams filled in admirably for Ewing, grabbing 19 rebounds, including 10 offensive. San Antonio played without long-injured centre David Robinson and guard Sean Elliott, who has tendinitis in his right quadricep.

In Charlotte, Anthony Mason scored 22 points, making all eight of his field-goal attempts, and Glen Rice added 17 points as the Hornets moved 10 games over the .500 mark for the first time this season with a 115-100 victory over the Sacramento Kings.
The Hornets won their fourth straight and matched a team record for three-pointers, hitting 14-for-23.
Mitch Richmond scored 37 points for the Kings, who lost the last two games of their four-game road trip.
In Orlando, Rony Seikaly had 32 points and Penny Hardaway 25 as the Magic won their fifth straight, 119-11 over the Boston Celtics.

Nick Anderson added 22 points for Orlando, which has won 12 of its last 14. Seikaly, who also grabbed 12 rebounds, has 52 points and 23 rebounds in his last two games. The Magic improved to 13-3 since Hardaway returned to the lineup.
The Magic outscored the Celtics 40-22 in the third period, their highest scoring quarter of the season.
Rick Fox scored 30 points and Todd Day added 25 for the Celtics, who have lost 10 of their last 12 games and fell to 2-18 on the road this season.
In New Jersey, Reggie Miller scored 26 points and Antonio Davis 18 as the Indiana Pacers beat the Nets 104-100.
Indiana has won four of its last five games.

Jayson Williams, who has postponed season-ending thumb surgery, came off the bench to record 21 points and 20 rebounds for New Jersey, which has lost six of eight. Shawn Bradley collected 14 points and 14 boards and tied a season high with 11 blocked shots.

In Minnesota, Kevin Garnett scored 18 points, Dean Garrett had 17 points and 13 rebounds and Tom Gugliotta also had 17 points as the Timberwolves cruised to their fourth win in five games, 103-86 over the Vancouver Grizzlies.
Anthony Peeler scored 24 points for the Grizzlies, who have lost 10 of their last 11 games.
